neighbours.label: the hedging interjection ', well,' set off mid-sentence before a blunt or understated description (it's, well, kind of weak), as opposed to sentence-initial 'Well,', the adverb 'well' and the noun 'well'
fire: The new sofa looks stylish, but sitting on it is, well, painful.
His speech was meant to inspire the team, but it came across as, well, a lecture.
We hired the cheapest movers because, well, we had no money left.
The soup tasted a bit too salty and, well, kind of bland too.
Her paintings are colourful, bold and—well, a little strange.
The hotel promised luxury, but the room was, well, tiny.
They named the dog Shadow because, well, he follows you everywhere.
The app works fine, but the design is, well, rather ugly.
quiet: Well, the new sofa looks stylish, but sitting on it is painful.
His speech was meant to inspire the team, and it worked well.
We hired the cheapest movers because we had no money left.
The soup tasted salty, but the bread went well with it.
Her paintings are colourful and bold, and they sell well.
The hotel stood next to an old stone well in the square.
They named the dog Shadow, a name that is well known in town.
The app works well, but the design is rather ugly.

predictions: fire 0.6-1.2 on ' well' between commas or after a dash mid-sentence; sentence-initial 'Well,', 'played well', 'well known' and 'a deep well' below 0.05
